ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human safety reviewer with the factual summary below; do not execute any fare action (the fixed RydeX quote of $24.64 stands, no off-route segment recorded), and have the reviewer read the driver's statement wording under SAFE-1 (driver conduct) alongside the rider's dangerous-driving allegation under SAFE-2; no account flag is supported on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
The ride was a fixed-quote RydeX trip from NUS to Raffles Place, $24.64, pickup 08:36 and drop-off 08:51 [F1]. The rider's complaint alleges speeding, hard braking the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder and that she felt scared and unsafe; that is a dangerous-driving allegation and SAFE-2 requires the case to be routed to a person rather than decided automatically. The trace confirms the screen has already marked this as a safety incident, so escalate is the only available outcome [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

The measurable records do not settle the allegation either way: the driven distance was 10.5 km against a 10.6 km optimal route (-0.1 km) and the trip took 15.9 min against a 16.5 min estimate [F1][F2]. Those aggregates are consistent with ordinary driving and show no off-route segment, so no route-deviation refund arises and no fare element is recoverable; but they record no speed profile, no braking events and no lane or shoulder information, so they cannot exclude brief speeding or hard braking inside an otherwise on-time trip. That gap is exactly why SAFE-2 sends the matter to a human [F1][F2][RD-1][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

On the second safety element, reading F6 in context: the driver's post-trip statement says "The rider is stupid and was on the phone the whole trip. I drove normally." The words "stupid" and the phone accusation are hostile remarks aimed at the rider; under Ryde's Code of Conduct, which bars abuse of any kind, and reading the words themselves rather than a keyword, this is at least a suspected abuse-of-the-rider issue for the reviewer to assess under SAFE-1, and it also conflicts with the complete, fully timestamped chat record, which shows only the pickup arrangement and no mention of phone use [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1]. I do not decide it here; the record goes to a person.

The chat contains no contemporaneous report of dangerous driving during the ride, and no traffic facts exist to corroborate or rebut the allegation; I treat the absence of corroboration as a gap, not as evidence for the driver [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-2]. Since neither party's profile may decide the case and neither party has a record of repeated violations, no account flag attaches to either side [F7][F8][RD-6]. The fare is a fixed RydeX quote with no challenged add-on, so nothing monetary is ordered and the amount is left null [F1][FARE-1].
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety case: the rider alleges speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking and states she felt scared and unsafe (SAFE-2); additionally the driver's post-trip statement calls the rider "stupid" and claims phone use that the complete chat record does not show (SAFE-1, suspected abuse). The objective record is silent on the driving conduct, so a human reviewer must weigh the rider's first-hand account against the neutral aggregate records.

rejected_claims.reason: The absence of telematics or video does not defeat the allegation; SAFE-2 requires escalation precisely because the record does not settle a dangerous-driving claim, and the requested no_action is not an available outcome. The gap is treated as missing evidence, not as evidence for the driver [F1][F2][SAFE-2].
The absence of an off-route segment in F1 answers only the route-deviation question (RD-1); it says nothing about speed, braking or shoulder use, which is what was alleged [F1][RD-1][SAFE-2].

An aggregate duration 0.6 min under the estimate (F2) is consistent with ordinary driving but cannot exclude bursts of speeding or hard braking inside the trip; the record carries no speed profile [F2][SAFE-2].

The complete timestamped chat record F3/F4/F5 shows no contemporaneous safety report, but silence during the ride is not proof the driving was safe; and F6's assertion that the rider was on the phone the whole trip is a driver statement contradicted by the chat record, which contains no such exchange [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

Characterising F6 as mere discourtesy is not the driver's call; the word stupid and the phone accusation are hostile remarks aimed at the rider and must be read by the reviewer under the Code's bar on abuse of any kind (SAFE-1) [F6][SAFE-1].
A clean profile (F8) cannot decide whether an unrecorded dangerous-driving incident occurred; profile facts never decide a case, and no account action is sought in any event [F7][F8][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Accepted in effect: the conceded point that neither party's clean 90-day history supports an account flag aligns with RD-6, which requires an upheld violation and a prior upheld route dispute; neither exists here, so no flag is applied [F7][F8][RD-6].

Accepted in effect: the fixed RydeX quote of $24.64 with no challenged add-on means no refund is ordered under FARE-1; but this cannot produce a clean no_action while a safety screen is outstanding [F1][FARE-1][SAFE-2].

ruling.evidence_gap: The dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) has no supporting record: the chat is complete and timestamped but contains only the pickup arrangement with no contemporaneous safety report [F3][F4][F5], and the GPS/timeline facts give aggregate distance and duration only (10.5 km vs 10.6 km; 15.9 min vs 16.5 min), with no speed profile, harsh-braking event, lane/shoulder data or in-trip location trace that could confirm or exclude it [F1][F2]. No traffic facts exist in the record.
